geometry.leash: constraint relative to an anchor; only when admissible motion is actually restricted
geometry.cage: intersection of multiple boundaries/constraints, not automatically one literal wall

relationship_model.entanglement: structured relational dependence, coupling, correlation, topology, feedback and path dependence
relationship_model.constraint: restriction on admissible states or trajectories; may be hard, soft, causal, legal, topological, resource or model-specific
relationship_model.leash: project constraint metaphor requiring anchor, constrained degree of freedom, active condition and exit/release rule
relationship_model.trajectory: ordered state evolution through time under declared dynamics and constraints
relationship_model.timeline: one admissible history/path; a family of timelines is a path ensemble rather than automatically a physical multiverse
relationship_model.topology: connectivity, bridges, dominators, bottlenecks, cuts, cycles, winding, basins and attractors
relationship_model.reachability: states that can still be reached from a starting state under declared controls, disturbances and constraints
relationship_model.fate_destiny: interpretive umbrella that must be split into hard constraint, invariant, attractor, absorbing state, probability-one target, all-path target, reachable target or theological destiny before analysis

fate_tests.possible: EF target / at least one admissible path reaches target
fate_tests.inevitable: AF target / every admissible path reaches target in the declared model
fate_tests.invariant: AG safe-set / all admissible paths stay inside declared set
fate_tests.probabilistic: P(hit target before failure) under a specified stochastic model
fate_tests.absorbing: P_aa=1 in a declared Markov model
fate_tests.theological: providence, election, predestination or telos; never silently converted into mechanics

canonical_transformations.note: relationship grammar applied to observable systems
relations can have distance, coupling, feedback, topology and trajectories
some relations restrict admissible states/paths while others merely correlate or enable
use leash only when anchor, restriction and release logic are explicit
timeline is represented as an admissible history through state/transition space
target-set is a neutral mathematical comparator, not proof of providence
